citation.sourceDocument: Nevada Department of Taxation, no state personal income tax
citation.sourceNote: A state with no income tax is a first-class record here, not an omission: the shard exists, carries a citation, and answers "nothing" deliberately rather than by having nothing to say. The caveat that matters is what a $0 state income tax does NOT mean. A state still has to fund itself, and the ones without an income tax generally lean harder on sales and property taxes — neither of which this engine models. So a take-home figure here is exactly right about state income tax and silent about the rest of the state's tax burden; comparing two states on this number alone will mislead you. Nevada levies no individual income tax, and Art. 10 §1(9) of the Nevada Constitution prohibits one. The state is funded largely by sales tax and by gaming and live-entertainment taxes, and employers pay a Modified Business Tax on wages that does not appear on an employee's pay stub.
